scenarios.scenario-1: Recorded graph payloads parse into exactly the expected file-level import edges: symbol endpoints and non-import relations dropped, duplicates collapsed, deterministic sort.
scenarios.scenario-2: Against a fake MCP server (same stdio protocol) the adapter returns deduped edges and per-file symbols; malformed JSON becomes an INTEGRATION_INVALID_OUTPUT note; a timeout becomes an INTEGRATION_TIMEOUT note.
scenarios.scenario-3: `impact --code-graph` maps edges to module DEPENDS: undeclared imports are info CODE_EDGE_UNDECLARED, declared-but-unimported edges are info DECLARED_EDGE_UNUSED, exit code unchanged. `trace --code` resolves MODULE_MAP entries and `--strict-contracts` turns a missing symbol into exit 1.
scenarios.scenario-4: Without Octocode every path degrades honestly: available:false + INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE info, no crash, no changed deterministic output; out-of-range versions never spawn a session.

required-log-markers.marker-1: No runtime log markers; behavior asserted through returned payloads and CLI JSON envelopes.

notes.note-1: Covered by test/grace-code-graph.test.ts (parsers + fake MCP server), plus the enrichment tests in test/grace-impact.test.ts and test/grace-trace.test.ts.
notes.note-2: Real-binary contract smoke is manual: `bun run test:integrations --download` (pinned 0.29.2); it is not a CI gate in v1.4.0 because the pinned binary did not answer MCP initialize on the dev host.
notes.note-3: ADR-9: read-only tools only, one short-lived session, capped notes/payloads, scrubbed env, external output never executed.
